title: Minimum Non-Zero Product of the Array Elements
summary: Given a positive integer p, an array nums is formed with integers from 1 to 2^p - 1.
statement: Given a positive integer p, an array nums is formed with integers from 1 to 2^p - 1. You can swap corresponding bits between any two elements in nums any number of times. The task is to find the minimum non-zero product of the array elements after performing these operations, and return this product modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: The initial multiset contains every integer from 1 through 2^p-1.
Swapping same-position bits preserves each bit column; minimize a nonzero product and return it modulo 1000000007.
reference_solution:
def minimum_nonzero_bit_swap_product(p):
    mod = 1_000_000_007
    maximum = (1 << p) - 1
    pairs = (maximum - 1) // 2
    return maximum % mod * pow(maximum - 1, pairs, mod) % mod

def minimum_nonzero_bit_swap_product(p):
    mod = 1_000_000_007
    maximum = (1 << p) - 1
    pairs = (maximum - 1) // 2
    return maximum % mod * pow(maximum - 1, pairs - 1, mod) % mod
hints: Pair each x with its bitwise complement: preserving one all-ones value lets every other pair become 1 and 2^p-2.
maximum=2^p-1; pairs=(maximum-1)//2; multiply maximum by modular_power(maximum-1,pairs).
For a fixed pair sum, pushing positive factors to 1 and sum-1 minimizes their product. Complement pairs have the needed conserved bits, while the all-ones value remains unpaired.
